page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n1 server family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 30.0 GB of dedicated system memory, translating to 3.75 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the n1-standard-8 delivers modest performance characteristics. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, falls into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, Geekbench scores place its single-core and multi-core capabilities in the poor and weak categories respectively, with text processing and decompression tasks showing lower efficiency. However, memory subsystem performance is relatively stronger, with large-block read and write memory bandwidths achieving average ratings. Ray tracing and small-model text generation also demonstrate average performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density suitable for legacy workloads or development environments where peak compute performance is not critical. Given the lack of local storage and lower CPU benchmark scores, this instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as basic web serving, lightweight application hosting, and moderate memory-bound tasks rather than intensive database operations or high-performance computing.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine from the n1 family, configured with 8 vCPUs and 30.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.3 GHz, it features 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs. Performance benchmarks indicate weak to poor single-core and multi-core CPU capabilities, though memory bandwidth for large blocks and text generation for small LLM models achieve average ratings. Given its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and moderate performance profile, the n1-standard-8 is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including basic web serving, software compilation, and development environments that require dedicated CPU allocation without demanding high-compute or high-I/O performance.
